recommendation.recommendation: Implement immediate flood irrigation to relieve severe water stress and sustain the high‑vigour rice canopy.
recommendation.justification: Satellite NDWI indicates critical water deficit (‑0.35) and there has been no recent rainfall. Soil health (score 92) and canopy greenness (NDVI 0.80) are excellent, meaning the crop can quickly recover if water is supplied. Market prices are stable to rising, so preserving yield now maximizes profitability.
actions: Activate flood irrigation across the entire field today, delivering 5‑7 cm of water per day for the next 5‑7 days (adjust to maintain soil moisture at 70‑80 % of field capacity).
After the first irrigation cycle, apply a balanced NPK fertilizer at the recommended rate for the vegetative stage.
Install soil‑moisture sensors (tensiometers or capacitance probes) at 15 cm depth and record readings twice daily to verify target moisture levels.
Conduct a visual disease scout each morning for blast, sheath blight, and leaf spot; record any symptoms and apply appropriate fungicide if needed.
Log irrigation volumes, fertilizer applications, and sensor data in a field notebook or digital app for traceability.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Restored soil moisture will prevent yield loss, maintain the current high NDVI, reduce disease susceptibility, and position the farmer to capture stable to increasing market prices, resulting in a profitable harvest.
monitoring_plan: Daily NDWI check via satellite or drone imagery (aim for NDWI ≥ 0.2).
Weekly NDVI assessment to confirm canopy health remains ≥ 0.7.
Soil‑moisture sensor alerts: trigger irrigation if moisture falls below 65 % of field capacity.
Weather forecast review each morning to anticipate any rain that could reduce irrigation needs.
Bi‑weekly disease scouting reports; initiate fungicide treatment if disease incidence exceeds 5 % of plants.
